stem: A client near the end of life has severe dyspnea that remains intolerable despite optimal palliative treatment. The family asks, 'If palliative sedation is used, does that mean the team is trying to cause death?' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Palliative sedation may deliberately lower consciousness to relieve otherwise refractory suffering; its intent is comfort and symptom relief, not to shorten life or cause death.
options.B: Palliative sedation is used mainly to shorten the dying process after symptoms become difficult to control.
options.C: Palliative sedation is routinely used for clients in the last days of life even when symptoms remain adequately controlled with other palliative measures.
options.D: Once palliative sedation is chosen, decisions about hydration, nutrition, and other life-sustaining treatments are automatically determined by the sedation decision.

rationale: A is correct. NCI defines palliative sedation as deliberate pharmacologic lowering of consciousness to relieve symptoms that are unacceptably distressing and refractory to optimal palliative-care interventions. NCI states that the goal is relief of intractable suffering and that the intent is not to shorten life; the NCI Dictionary likewise states that palliative sedation is not meant to shorten life or cause death. B is incorrect because intentionally causing or hastening death is not the goal of palliative sedation. C is incorrect because palliative sedation is reserved for selected refractory symptoms rather than routine use for every dying client. D is incorrect because NCI states that decisions about potentially life-sustaining treatments such as artificial hydration or nutrition are distinct from the decision to use palliative sedation and require separate review of goals, benefits, harms, and preferences.
educational_objective: Explain that palliative sedation is an end-of-life comfort intervention for otherwise refractory suffering, with deliberate lowering of consciousness directed toward symptom relief rather than intentionally shortening life or causing death.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Last Days of Life (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version; Last Days of Life (PDQ®) — Patient Version; NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms — palliative sedation
source_version_date: Current NCI PDQ and Dictionary resources accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: Last Days of Life HP PDQ — section 'Palliative Sedation': definition, goal of relieving intractable suffering, indications for refractory symptoms, intended level/duration, and subsection 'Role of potentially LSTs during palliative sedation' stating intent is relief rather than shortening life and LST decisions are distinct; Patient Version — 'Suffering and Palliative Sedation at the End of Life'; NCI Dictionary entry 'palliative sedation'.
source_claim_supported: Palliative sedation deliberately lowers consciousness to relieve extreme or refractory suffering when other treatment has not adequately controlled symptoms; its intent is comfort rather than shortening life or causing death; decisions about other life-sustaining treatments remain separate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort, detailed content page 36 (PDF page 39), 'Nonpharmacological Comfort Interventions': assess need for palliative care/symptom management or noncurative treatments; counsel regarding palliative care/symptom management; respect palliative/noncurative treatment choices; assist client in receiving appropriate end-of-life physical symptom management; evaluate outcomes of palliative care/symptom management or noncurative treatments.
correction_summary: Rebuilt and remapped the source item. The stale generic AAHPM homepage/position-statement dependence was removed in favor of current NCI end-of-life sources. The item now tests a family-facing nursing explanation, explicitly separates palliative sedation from intent to cause death, distinguishes it from routine sedation, and preserves separate decision-making for other life-sustaining treatments. Mapping was corrected from Psychosocial Integrity to Basic Care and Comfort based on the 2026 NCSBN palliative/end-of-life symptom-management content.
audit_findings: Fresh NCI HP PDQ directly defines palliative sedation as deliberate lowering of consciousness for unacceptably distressing symptoms refractory to optimal palliative care and states that its goal is relief of intractable suffering.
The NCI Dictionary directly states that palliative sedation is not meant to shorten life or cause death, eliminating ambiguity about clinical intent.

NCI explicitly states that decisions about artificial hydration, nutrition, and other potentially life-sustaining treatments are distinct from the sedation decision, making D uniquely incorrect without relying on a fabricated rule.

2026 NCSBN detailed content places palliative care/symptom management and appropriate end-of-life physical symptom management under Basic Care and Comfort; the prior Psychosocial mapping was corrected.
Independent adversarial review found no second answer, cueing, outdated-source dependence, unsupported legal generalization, source-locator defect, or unresolved conflict.
